title: Stretched VCF 9.0 architecture with back-in-time NSX convergence
prompt:
Build the production architecture artifact for the greenfield VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 deployment in `fixtures/greenfield.json` and the ordered migration plan for `fixtures/estate.json`. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report. Implement package `vcfarch`, expose `Build(scenarioPath, estatePath, snapshotPath string) (Architecture, error)`, and produce deterministic `architecture.json`; the checked-in artifact and `Build` result for the shipped inputs must match.

Before implementing the design, use the harness's own genuine network research tools to consult current, reachable Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, bill-of-materials, and upgrade-path sources for the component combinations and transitions involved. Fetch and read the underlying sources rather than relying only on search-result snippets. Record what you actually consulted in `research/sources.json` as an object with a non-empty `sources` array. Each source must contain exactly `title`, `publisher`, `url`, `accessedAt`, and `decisions`: the first four values identify the source and its YYYY-MM-DD access date, while `decisions` is a non-empty array of the compatibility or upgrade decisions it informed. Each `url` must be an official HTTPS URL on `broadcom.com` or one of its subdomains. Cite those URLs in your final response. Choose the searches and sources yourself; no particular query or URL is required. Do not substitute the bundled fixtures for live research. Live material is research context only: `compatibility/vcf-9.0.0-snapshot.json` is the pinned grading authority if Broadcom's live matrix has changed. Verification checks the research record deterministically without making network calls.

`architecture.json` must contain `schemaVersion`, `greenfield`, and `existingEstate`. `greenfield.sddcSpec` must be an `SddcSpec` that validates against `components.schemas.SddcSpec` in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, vendored from tag `9.0.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Use only the inventoried hosts and pinned 9.0.0.0 bill of materials. Assign all eight data hosts to the two specified site fault domains, keep the dedicated witness in the independent witness site and out of `sddcSpec.hostSpecs`, carry every requested network and infrastructure value, use the required stretched vSAN ESA topology, and calculate the per-site capacity and headroom proving that either data site can run the stated workload after loss of the other. Model the stretched-cluster topology and witness placement alongside `sddcSpec`, because the installer schema does not express them.

`existingEstate.migrationPlan` must validate against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. Include every inventoried component exactly once, in strict contiguous execution order, with its inventory name, current version, pinned target, method, and all pinned gates. The estate's NSX 4.2.1.3 build is newer than the NSX 4.2.1.0 build in its required VCF 5.2.1 convergence bundle: do not model that as a downgrade or ordinary upgrade. Preserve the snapshot's skip-through-convergence disposition and then its forward lifecycle target. Also preserve management-plane-first/core-SDDC ordering, the fresh installation for the Logs transition, deferred NSX finalization, and witness-before-data-host sequencing.

Use only the Go standard library and keep `Build` safe for concurrent callers. Do not modify the fixtures, compatibility snapshot, schemas, installer specification, license, verifier, tests, or `go.mod`. Run `python3 verify.py`; it validates the SddcSpec against the installer specification's own schema before any other design check and then runs the table-driven tests with `go test -race ./...`.

research.subject: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 compatibility, interoperability, bill of materials, stretched-cluster witness placement, and the 5.2.1-to-9.0 upgrade path
research.verification_boundary: Verification checks the recorded source structure and official Broadcom HTTPS provenance without making network calls; the pinned compatibility snapshot is authoritative for the architecture artifact.
